biography.plain_text: King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al Saud ruled Saudi Arabia from 2005 until his death in 2015. A son of founder King Abdulaziz, he pursued cautious reforms that widened women's public participation, education and interfaith dialogue. As Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, he led an absolute monarchy central to Arab and Islamic affairs.

long_biography.plain_text:
Abdullah spent decades leading the Saudi Arabian National Guard, reshaping a tribal force into a central pillar of the state. As crown prince, he assumed daily management of state affairs after King Fahd's illness, then succeeded him as monarch. His Arab Peace Initiative called for a sovereign Palestinian state with East Jerusalem as its capital.

Education and dialogue became defining themes of his reign. He founded the coeducational King Abdullah University of Science and Technology, expanded overseas scholarships and convened interfaith meetings outside the kingdom. He appointed women to the Shura Council and said they could vote and stand in municipal elections. The changes were gradual, but they widened participation within a deeply conservative political order.
